params.body:
## What

Two read-only tools on the `portal` MCP server, with their doors in `lib/doors.mjs`:

- **`vulnerabilities`** (`slug`, optional `runtime`, `minimum`): one project's last vulnerability scan, by package. Each package comes with its version, ecosystem, lockfile, whether the site runs it, its advisories, its worst severity, the version that fixes it and whether that fix crosses a major. The tool also returns the packages flagged as malware, the commit that was scanned, when it was scanned, and Elixir's verdicts.
- **`affected`** (`pkg` or `advisory`): which projects run a vulnerable package or carry an advisory, at which version, in which lockfile. Projects whose scan did not measure are listed separately under `notLooked` and are never counted as safe.

## Why

A vulnerability task in the fleet brief reads "a critical vulnerability in a package the site runs (1)" and stops there. An agent that wants to act on it, or answer "which package?", had no command for it. Elixir already records the exact package, version and lockfile on every scan (`Scans\Vulnerabilities::describe`). This makes that record readable.

## Authority

- Blast radius B1. Both tools read only and say so in their description. They measure nothing, fix nothing and write nothing.
- No new door and no new scope. Both use Elixir's data that `reports/elixirData` already serves to the read token and to signing hands (`hand-read`). The tools pass on only the `vuln` section. The rest of the payload (credentials inventory, servers, deploys) stays in the client.
- `unavailable`, `notApplicable` and a missing section keep their state and note. They have no package list, rather than an empty one.

## Tested

- `node --test` in `mcp/`: four new tests (exact fields per package, the runtime and severity filters, a project that was never scanned, a fleet-wide match by package and by advisory). The response is also checked to carry nothing beyond the vuln section.
- The suite shows 10 passing and 2 failing. The two failures (`brief, measure and playbook…`, `tasks lists one project…`) already fail on `origin/main`: they mock the old direct POST routes, while `measure` and `task` now go through the gateway. This PR doesn't touch them.
- A read-only run against live Portal from the workbench: the Gentells pipeline returns `proxy-addr@2.0.7` CRITICAL (fixed in 2.0.8), `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` and `sharp@0.35.4` HIGH. `affected` for `proxy-addr` finds the same version in `vera`.

## Not in this PR

A narrower Portal door (vuln section only, admission-gated per project) is the least-privilege follow-up. It changes Portal's behaviour, so it waits for a separate go.
params.title: Read what a vulnerability scan found: each package, version and fix
